newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scandal-hit Belgians more optimistic for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Scandal-hit Belgians more optimistic for 1997.

text.p: Belgians, still reeling from child sex scandals which erupted in the second half of 1996, are more optimistic for the year ahead than 12 months ago, a poll published on Wednesday showed.
The Dimarso poll of 1,018 people, carried by the Belga agency, showed 39 percent expected the new year to be better, compared with just 24 percent in a similar poll last year.

Belgium, an affluent kingdom of 10 million with a respectable reputation, had an 'annus horribilis' in 1996 when it was hit first by a child sex and murder case and later by a paedophile affair in which one of its deputy prime ministers, Elio Di Rupo, was named before being cleared.

The bodies of four girls have been found in connection with the child murder case, dubbed the Dutroux affair after chief suspect Marc Dutroux, while two others were rescued alive but had been sexually abused. Police are still searching for seven Di Rupo was cleared by parliament last month of a series of allegations he had indulged in sex with boys under the legal age of consent of 16 years.
But a Christian Democratic minister in the country's Walloon regional government, Jean-Pierre Grafe, has resigned in the face of similar allegations.

The poll showed that younger Belgians were more optimistic than older compatriots. Fifty-two percent of the category up to the age of 34 anticipated a better year against 37 percent for those up to 54 and just 27 percent for the group above 55.
Fifty-three percent expect the jobless rate of 13.5 percent, one of the highest in Europe, to rise further in 1997. Women are more pessimistic than men regarding employment -- 58 percent against 48.
About 45 percent said their financial situation remained unchanged in 1996 but 33 percent said it worsened considerably.
